beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process reads and updates windowed features across shared recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: ThinkSR end to end: encoder, windows, shared DQ-CTM ticks, decoder.
beats.narration: The method keeps spatial detail in a carrier while the thought process stays compact. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing groups the feature field without discarding its tokens. The DQ-CTM thought process runs recurrent ticks with shared parameters. The decoder turns the updated dense carrier back into the super-resolved image. The recurrence returns to the thought stage itself, not around the full pipeline.

params.headline: ThinkSR separates dense output from compact thought
params.note: The loop belongs to the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier equation defines a dense feature field from the low-resolution image, then partitions that field into windows while keeping every token.
beats.narration: The equation makes the dense carrier explicit before the compact process operates on it. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into the feature field. The window partition operates on that field, keeping the tokens available for later updates.

params.headline: The dense carrier is encoded before it is windowed

terms.label: window partition keeps the feature tokens

beats.intent: Across the five reported methods, DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model; its 1.129 million parameters are the second largest.
beats.claim: DQ-CTM-SR has 1.129M parameters in Table 1, compared with CATANet 0.535M, RFDN 0.550M, IMDN 0.715M, and CARN 1.592M.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should be read as a cost, not only as a result. CATANet is the smallest reported model at 0.535 million parameters. RFDN is nearly the same size at 0.550 million. IMDN is larger at 0.715 million. DQ-CTM-SR reaches 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is the largest baseline at 1.592 million parameters.

params.headline: DQ-CTM-SR is the second largest model here
params.note: Smallest first; average scores are not shown.
